info:
The important pattern is:

Verb (plain) + つもりはない

= have no intention of doing

So the verb stays in the plain positive form even though the overall construction is negative:

料理するつもりはない
"don't intend to cook"

That makes this different from simply negating the verb:

料理しない
"don't/won't cook"

The latter is a general negative, while 料理するつもりはない specifically emphasizes lack of intention.
